7. What the access model now covers

The architecture removes hidden interior field fasteners. The robot approaches from the exterior, withdraws to transit planes at 
∣

∣y∣=1.00 m, and makes long translations there.

The calculation includes the carried member, cradle, cutter, wrist, cable allowances, structural motion and stopping reserves. It uses continuous swept prisms, enclosing rotation discs, and the convex hull of the complete 5 mm saddle-release lift.

The final access execution gives:

Access quantity	Result
Whole-member routes	108
Endpoint approaches	216
Station routes	21
Minimum settled normal-route clearance	9.782 mm
Minimum clearance through complete lift/withdrawal	5.719 mm
Minimum local corridor allowance	1.5 mm
Upper-platform stopping clearance	60.56 mm

A separate stationary neighboring-body calculation uses 12.31 mm translation and 26 mrad rotation. It passes narrowly, with only 0.362 mm minimum projected clearance.

However, the own host-node/captured-nose relative cutting transition remains unqualified. The full stationary-cut/extraction certificate is therefore false.

Other access omissions are explicit:

The four-face in-place ultrasonic scan is still an event contract; the route model does not provide all four probe approaches.
Cradle takeover, fork-gap observation, keeper operation and restrained rack deenergization lack qualified installed response maps.
The platform’s internal gearbox/motor packing and loaded stopping behavior remain unqualified.

Thus the new model improves substantially on incomplete endpoint searches, but it does not supply the complete physically executed access operation.
